column2: How do I keep several ways of setting up animals, or move them to another computer?
column3: Settings → Animals → “💾 Saved settings”: “💾 Save under a name…” gives them a name (e.g. Horse breeding); choose one and “Apply” to go back to it. “⤓ Export” makes a .json file (the settings and all the sets); “⤒ Import” takes it into another database.

column2: Where do the photos and notes of an animal with a full record go?
column3: In its record, as for a person: its photos and documents (paper pedigree, health book…) in the “Media” block, its notes and sources in the “Notes” block. Those from the old animal record were moved there: nothing is lost.

column2: How do I make the pedigree (the tree) of a pedigree animal?
column3: In the animal’s record, choose its sire and dam if they have a record (otherwise write their name and registration). “🌳 Pedigree” shows 2 to 8 generations (sire’s side at the top, dam’s side at the bottom); an ancestor who appears several times has its own colour. The inbreeding coefficient (Wright’s coefficient, from the known ancestors) and the common ancestors are shown; the pedigree can be printed or downloaded as a spreadsheet. The record also shows the offspring by litter and the siblings (same parents or half). “＋ A young one” creates the record of a young animal with this parent already filled in.

column2: Where do I set the colours, shapes, arrowheads, fonts and menus of boards?
column3: Settings → “Boards”. Colours: the swatches offered for each use (fill, border, text, drawing, notes, board background), in the order you want, with several possible palettes. Arrowheads: those offered and their order, and the default arrowhead at the start and end. Shapes: the order of categories and shapes, those to hide, quick access. Fonts: font lists of your own (with the computer’s fonts). Sizes: from which to which thickness (0.5 to 500 px) and text size (up to 500 px), the default rounding. Spreadsheet: how it looks when placed. Brushes: your own, with their hardness. Menus and options: the order (or hiding) of the tools, the top buttons, the settings on the right and the “Add” menu. At the top of the page, “💾 Save under a name…” keeps all these settings together (like an Appearance design); “My saved settings” → “Apply” to go back to them, 🗑 to delete them.

column2: How do I set the caption of a line or an arrow?
column3: Choose the line: on the right, write the “Caption”, then “Caption settings”: size, font, bold, italic, text colour, frame (fill, border, border thickness, padding, rounding; “transparent” fill for no frame), position along the line (0 % at the start, 100 % at the end), side (on the line, above, below), distance from the line, and “follow the angle of the line” to tilt it like the line.

column2: How do I choose and arrange the quick-access shapes?
column3: Settings → Boards → Shapes: ⚡ on a shape adds it to quick access (the shapes offered directly in the bar of the Shapes tool); in “Quick access”, drag a shape or use ‹ › to change the order, × to remove it. Don’t forget “Save”.

column2: Where do I find the letters, numbers, coats of arms, frames and other shapes for boards?
column3: In a board: Shapes tool (⬠) → “All shapes”. The library has nearly 5,000 shapes: the whole alphabet (A to Z, a to z, accented letters É È À Ç…, digits and numbers, punctuation), each alone, in a circle, in a circle (outline), in a square or in a square (outline); genealogy signs (° birth, † death, ⚭ marriage, ∞, parent → children links, braces); shields and divisions of coats of arms (per pale, per fess, quarterly, chevron, cross…); frames and friezes; labels and ribbons; simplified flags to colour; occupations, tools, animals, buildings, transport, weather, music, sport, emotions… Type a word in the box (without worrying about accents: “eglise”, “flags”, “É”); the filters at the top give the number found per kind (Tab moves from one to the next); ↑ ↓ ← → then Enter to take it. The extra shapes load the first time it is opened (a short moment), not at start-up. A shape placed stays in the board as it is.

column2: The “All fonts” window doesn’t show all my fonts: what should I do?
column3: In the app installed on the computer, the full list of fonts is shown directly. In a browser (Chrome, Edge), click “🔓 See all the computer’s fonts”: the browser asks for permission once. If you refused, open the site settings (the padlock to the left of the address) → “Fonts” → Allow, then reopen the window. Safari and Firefox do not give the list: the app shows the common fonts it finds, and you can type the exact name of another font. The fonts appear little by little as you scroll down, each written in its own font.

column2: How do I choose the colour of what I place in a board?
column3: As soon as a tool has colours, the top bar shows the swatches of your palette and, at the end, an “other colour” square to choose one freely: Text (text colour), Note (note fill), Shapes (fill), Line and Arrow (line colour), Drawing. For an arrow, “Arrowheads” gives the arrowheads a separate colour (“=”: like the line). Once the item is placed, everything can be changed on the right, including “Arrowhead colour”.

column2: How do I change the order of the Settings pages?
column3: At the bottom of the Settings column, next to “Archive room”: “Reorder”. Drag a line, or use its arrows ↑ ↓, then Save; “↺ Reset to default” puts back the original order. (The order can also be set in Appearance.)

column2: Where are the glossary and the FAQ?
column3: In Settings, two pages: “Glossary” (genealogy vocabulary, old occupations, help reading records, your personal dictionary) and “FAQ / guide” (quick pointers and these frequently asked questions, with the “Ask your question” search). A button at the top of each page leads to the other.

column2: How do I underline, strike through, or make a bulleted or numbered list in a board?
column3: Choose the text, note or shape: on the right, B (bold), I (italic), U (underline), S (strikethrough), then align left, centre, right, justify. “Bullets and numbers”: bullet, 1. 2. 3., I. II. III., a. b. c., A. B. C., dash, checkboxes — one line = one item. “Font” offers your font lists; 🖥 adds the computer’s fonts; you can also type a name.

column2: How do I get more shapes, or create my own?
column3: Shapes tool (S) → “All shapes ▾”: nearly 800 shapes arranged in 23 categories (basic, geometry, arrows, bubbles, stars, symbols, genealogy, people, beliefs and memory, writings and documents, places, house and objects, clothes, occupations and tools, transport, animals, nature, weather, cooking, music games and sport, health…), with a search. “＋ Create a shape”: with the pen (as in Photoshop: click = corner point, click and drag = smooth point with its handles, click on the first point = closed shape, ⌥ / Alt for independent handles, a path inside the shape = a hole), from a drawing in the board or from an image. “🧩 From a shape”: take a shape, flip it (mirror, upside down), rotate it, stretch it, add other shapes to it or cut holes in it, and give it a name (also with ✏️ on the right on a placed shape, or on each shape in Settings → Boards → Shapes). Your shapes go into “My shapes” and into quick access.

column2: How do I export, print, import a board?
column3: At the top of the board: “⤓ Export” → PNG or JPG image, PDF, Print…, the selection as PNG, or “Board file” (.lcnda-tableau.json). For the file, two choices: “Light, without the photos” (small, easy to send, perfect in the same database; elsewhere the missing photos become notes) or “Complete, with the photos” (heavier, but complete everywhere: on import, the missing photos, sounds and PDFs are added to the database). “＋ Add → Import a board” reopens this file as a new board; the links are kept when it is the same database. The zoom (the percentage) has a menu: fit to selection, fit content to the window, 50 / 100 / 200 %.

column2: How do I merge spreadsheet cells?
column3: Click a cell, then ⇧ + click on another: the cells between the two are selected. On the right: “⊞ Merge” (the texts are joined end to end in the first), “⊟ Split” to undo it; the fill is applied to all the selected cells.

column2: Which brushes and erasers are there in a board?
column3: ✍︎ tool (P), then the brush button: Pen, Monoline, Marker, Pencil (grain), Pastel, Fountain pen (the line gets thinner when you go fast), Reed pen (bevelled tip), Brush, Watercolour, Fill (the traced shape is filled), Highlighter, Chalk, Neon, Airbrush, Dotted. At the top of the menu, five ready-made thicknesses; next to them, the exact thickness in px and a colour of your choice. ⌫ tool (E): “Fine eraser” erases only what it touches (the line is cut), with its size in px; “Stroke eraser” removes the whole line. A drawing already made can change brush in the right panel.

column2: How do I put a spreadsheet in a board?
column3: ▦ tool (G) then click, or “＋ Add” → A spreadsheet. Double-click a cell to write; Enter goes down, Tab moves to the next one (and adds a row at the end), Esc cancels. Formulas: =B2+B3, =SOMME(B2:B9), =MOYENNE, =MIN, =MAX, =NB, =PRODUIT, =ARRONDI(B2;1)… (English names such as SUM also work). Paste a piece of Excel or Numbers into a cell: it fits into the grid. On the right: add or remove rows and columns, column width, header row and column, every other row shaded, cell fill, download as CSV.

column2: How do I see what is grouped in a board?
column3: Each group has a coloured dotted frame and a badge “Group n · number of items”: click the badge to select the whole group (and move it by dragging). The ⧉ button near the zoom shows or hides the frames.

column2: How do I take a snapshot of a board, or make a new board from another one?
column3: At the top of the board: “📸 Snapshots” freezes the board as it is (give it a name). Later, “Go back to this state” (the current state is kept as a snapshot first, nothing is lost), or “Make it a board” to create a separate one. “⧉ Copy” immediately creates a new board with the current content, with or without the same arrangement. In addition, the app automatically keeps one “⏱ automatic version” per working day (the last 30), stored separately and folded at the bottom of the list of snapshots.

column2: How do I place an automatic tree in a board?
column3: “＋ Add” → “🌳 An automatic tree”: choose the person, then their ancestors, their descendants or their close family (parents, siblings, spouses, children), the number of generations, with or without spouses, arrows or lines. The records are placed linked and grouped (next to what is already there); each card stays linked to its record: double-click to open it.

column2: How do I put a timeline or a map in a board?
column3: “＋ Add” → “🗓 A live timeline”: a person’s dated events (or those of their couple and children) place themselves on a time line, and follow the record. “🗺 A map”: the places of a person, their family or the person of an investigation; on the right, “Place a marker” adds your own points (a commune, a place), and “link the places in order” draws the route.
